shower.thought: # Shower Thoughts
We spend years learning to read, but no one teaches us how to stop reading into things.
Your phone knows more about your future than you do.
The only time you see yourself is when you're looking at a mirror or a photo, which means you've never actually seen yourself—only your reflection or a captured moment.
Boredom might be your brain's way of telling you that you're not learning anything new, which means boredom is a skill you're forgetting to use.
You'll never know if you're colorblind unless you compare your colors to someone else's, and there's no way to verify you're seeing the same thing anyway.
Every conversation ends, but you never know if it's the last time you'll talk to that person.
Time moves slower when you're waiting for something because your brain has nothing to file away as memories—boredom erases itself.
We celebrate people for "following their passion," but passion is just obsession that worked out.
The saddest part of growing up isn't losing wonder; it's realizing how much of childhood was just low expectations disguised as magic.
You can't actually prove you have consciousness—you just assume everyone else does too.
Money is just a collective agreement that something is valuable, but we treat it like an objective truth.
Silence is uncomfortable because it gives your brain a chance to talk to itself.
We're all just trying to make sense of a instruction manual we never asked for.
The reason we find symmetry beautiful might just be because our brains are lazy and symmetry requires less processing power.
You've probably had the thought that would change your life, but you forgot it because you thought it wasn't important enough to remember.
Grief is just love with nowhere to go.
Everyone you know is the villain in someone else's story.
We're afraid of missing out, but we're actively missing out on the present moment while thinking about what we might be missing.
Your worst enemy and your best friend could have the exact same personality—the only difference is your history with them.

darkjoke.thought:
My therapist asked why I think everyone hates me.
I said, "You're getting paid to listen, so your opinion doesn't count."

I told my friend he was living in denial.
He said, "No I'm not." We haven't spoken since.

My parents said they'd always be there for me.
Turns out they meant emotionally unavailable, not physically present.

I asked the suicide hotline if things get better.
The guy said, "Dude, I've been on hold for three hours."

My doctor told me I have six months to live.
I said I couldn't afford the bill.
He said, "Okay, you have a year."

I started going to the gym to improve my mental health.
Now I'm just depressed and sore.

My ex said she needed space.
I gave her the whole apartment and moved into my car.
Turns out that's not what she meant.

I told my boss I had imposter syndrome.
He said, "Don't worry, you're not an imposter."
That was somehow worse.

At my intervention, everyone said I drink too much.
I said, "At least I'm consistent at something."

My mom asked if I was seeing anyone special.
I said, "Yeah, a grief counselor."
She didn't laugh. I wasn't joking.

I went to a self-help seminar titled "Find Your Purpose."
Turns out my purpose was paying $200 to sit in a hotel ballroom.

My friend said he was going through a rough patch.
I said, "Hang in there."
He's still mad I said that while he was on a ladder.

I told my date I was really into dark humor.
She said, "That explains why you're here alone."

My bank account has more zeros than my dating life.
At least one of them represents actual value.

I asked my Uber driver if he liked his job.
He said, "Honestly? I drive people around and regret every decision that led here."
I said, "That's oddly specific."
He said, "I was talking about my life."

My therapist said I need to work on my self-esteem.
I said, "Thanks for noticing I don't have any."
She didn't correct me.

I went to a networking event to make connections.
I left with three business cards and zero self-respect.
Two of those cards were for pizza places.

My friend asked if I believed in second chances.
I said, "Not really."
He said, "Good, because you're not getting one."

My doctor said I need to be more positive.
I said, "Okay, I'm positive I'm going to die."
He prescribed me antidepressants.
I think he won.
